subject.title: [Bug]: Session write-lock held beyond run lifetime when agent run fails during tool execution

question: Which open session-lock PR should own the alive same-process retained-lock failure reported here, and what lock-reclaim boundary is acceptable before merge?
rationale: The issue is a valid bug, but the open candidate PRs propose different recovery policies with session-state compatibility risk, and one candidate targets dead-PID behavior that does not match the alive PID evidence.

options.title: Review alive-holder teardown fix
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100870 or a narrowed equivalent as the primary path, after fixing its review blockers and adding real recovery proof.

options.title: Retarget dead-PID hardening
options.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100878 only as dead-PID hardening and remove its closing relationship to this alive-holder issue unless further proof shows it fixes this report.

options.title: Consolidate broader lock policy
options.body: Fold this issue into the older live-holder maxHold/reclaim discussion around https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87483 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/89673 if maintainers want one shared reclaim contract.

recommendation.title: Review alive-holder teardown fix
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100870 or a narrowed equivalent as the primary path, after fixing its review blockers and adding real recovery proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the embedded-attempt session lock lifecycle and watchdog/cleanup code that determines the safe fix boundary.
